inputs.spec_clause_ref: kerml clause 8.2.5.7.1 (Functions.md, region_sha256 f8fd09bcff0e258a) | sysml clause 8.2.2.19 (CalculationsTextualNotation.md, region_sha256 ee541841395079da)

decision: A member prefix and an expression, and nothing else — no keyword, and in particular no terminating semicolon. That missing semicolon is the whole production: it is what distinguishes the result expression of a body from a member of it, and it is why FunctionBodyPart can admit at most one and only in final position.
notes:
split per language (ADR-0014): KerML and SysML state this production differently, so it is derived as one variant per language instead
THE TWO CLAUSES DIFFER BY ONE CHARACTER AND IT IS NOT A CONFLICT. KerML 8.2.5.7.1 writes `MemberPrefix ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression`; SysML 8.2.2.19 writes `MemberPrefix? ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression`. MemberPrefix is `( visibility = VisibilityIndicator )?` and therefore already derives the empty string, so `MemberPrefix?` and `MemberPrefix` accept exactly the same text. The languages agree on what parses and the `?` is redundant, not contradictory, so this is recorded rather than adjudicated. Written without the `?`, following KerML, which the Xtext also agrees with.

FOR A PARSER AUTHOR: this production is two nullable-or-not references and contributes no terminal of its own, so it cannot be recognised by lookahead at its start. It is recognised by its position — last in a FunctionBodyPart — and by what follows it, which is the body's closing `}` rather than a `;`. A parser that commits to a member on seeing an expression will have to be able to reconsider when the semicolon does not arrive.

CORPUS: the context pack reported no instances, and that is a limitation of the matcher rather than a fact about the language. The matcher keys on terminals, and this production has none. But an instance IS identifiable by position — the trailing semicolon-less expression in a function body — and one is cited below. A first draft of this unit claimed no corpus text was attributable to this production; that claim was wrong and has been removed.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE: the SysML clause reaches this production through CalculationBodyPart and pairs it with ReturnParameterMember, where KerML pairs it with ReturnFeatureMember. Those are two differently-named productions and belong to their own units.

evidence.note: ResultExpressionMember is stated there as MemberPrefix followed by OwnedExpression
states the same production with a redundant `?` on the already-nullable MemberPrefix
the pilot rule is MemberPrefix then OwnedExpression, without the `?`. SysML.xtext writes it the same way, so the pilot treated the SysML clause's `?` as redundant too.

`function TotalMass { in partMass; in subparts; partMass + (...) }` — the trailing expression carries no semicolon before the closing brace, which is this production and nothing else. It substantiates the claim in the notes that the production is recognised by position rather than by lookahead.
